{{Short description|American chemist and educator}}

'''Richard P. Van Duyne''' (1945–2019) was an American chemist and professor of chemistry at [[Northwestern University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pathbreaking chemist Richard P. Van Duyne dies |url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2019/08/pathbreaking-chemist-richard-p-van-duyne-dies/ |access-date=July 27, 2023 |website=Northwestern Now}}</ref> He was known for his development of [[surface-enhanced Raman scattering|surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)]] and [[nanophotonics|nanoplasmonics]] initially for analytical and [[physical chemistry]], but the high sensitivity of these methods resulted in numerous applications in chemistry, [[materials science and engineering]], [[physics]], and medicine. He definitively demonstrated the single molecule sensitivity of SERS.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dieringer |first1=Jon A. |last2=Lettan |first2=Robert B. |last3=Scheidt |first3=Karl A. |last4=Van Duyne |first4=Richard P. |date=2007 |title=A Frequency Domain Existence Proof of Single-Molecule Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ja077243c |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc. |volume=129 |issue=51 |pages=16249–16256 |doi=10.1021/ja077243c|pmid=18052068 |bibcode=2007JAChS.12916249D |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Van Duyne was recognized by numerous awards, including the [[Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy]] of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[E. Bright Wilson Award in Spectroscopy]] and the Analytical Chemistry Award of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACS Award in Analytical Chemistry Recipients |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-award-in-analytical-chemistry/past-recipients.html |access-date=2023-07-27 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> He was also elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. In 2008, he received the Ellis R. Lippincott Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Richard P. Van Duyne (1945-2019): Department of Chemistry - Northwestern University |url=https://chemistry.northwestern.edu/people/in-memoriam/richard-van-duyne.html |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=chemistry.northwestern.edu |language=en}}</ref> After he passed away in 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-05 |title=Richard Van Duyne, Northwestern chemistry professor who studied information transfer via minuscule structures, dies |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2019/09/05/richard-van-duyne-northwestern-chemistry-professor-who-studied-information-transfer-via-minuscule-structures-dies/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> ACS published a special edition list of some of his publications,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Remembering Dr. Richard P. Van Duyne |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/vi/remembering-van-duyne |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=pubs.acs.org}}</ref> and some of his colleagues wrote articles about his work.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schatz |first=George C. |date=February 2021 |title=SERS and the scientific career of Richard P. Van Duyne (1945–2019) |url=https://analyticalsciencejournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jrs.6052 |journal=Journal of Raman Spectroscopy |language=en |volume=52 |issue=2 |pages=268–278 |doi=10.1002/jrs.6052 |issn=0377-0486}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cook |first=Kathleen |date=2019-08-01 |title=Pathbreaking chemist Richard P. Van Duyne dies |url=https://www.iinano.org/pathbreaking-chemist-richard-p-van-duyne-dies/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=International Institute for Nanotechnology |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Frontiera |first=Renee R. |last2=Haynes |first2=Christy L. |date=2019-11-12 |title=Richard P. Van Duyne, plasmonics pioneer |url=https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1915111116 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=116 |issue=46 |pages=22891–22893 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1915111116 |pmc=6859349 |pmid=31636203}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nie |first=Shuming |date=2020-01-28 |title=Remembering Dr. Richard P. Van Duyne (1945–2019): Gentleman, Scholar, and Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Pioneer |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.9b09759 |journal=ACS Nano |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=26–27 |doi=10.1021/acsnano.9b09759 |issn=1936-0851|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
